bottleneck.description: Heavy-payload (20kg+) collaborative robot arms - a niche where Doosan leads but where Universal Robots (UR20), FANUC (CRX-25iA) and ABB now offer direct substitutes.

dependency.key_customers: Auto OEMs, palletizing/machine-tending end users, distributors in North America/Western Europe (~70% of revenue overseas); recent ONExia acquisition (Pennsylvania integrator, July 2025) expands U.S. channel
dependency.key_suppliers: Servo motors, harmonic reduction gears (Nabtesco/Harmonic Drive/Leaderdrive), encoders, controllers, MCUs - all multi-sourced commodities

editorial.notes: Cobot market is structurally fragmented and competitive: Universal Robots (~15% share) leads, with Dobot, AUBO, JAKA, FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Techman and Franka Emika all viable alternatives. Doosan is a relatively strong number 5 globally (~4-5% share) and a leader in the 20kg+ niche, but FANUC CRX-25iA and UR20 directly compete. This sits with the calibration anchors ABBN/6954 JP/6503 JP/ROK as a peer-competitive industrial automation vendor. The cobot arm itself is increasingly a commodity; durable advantage rests in software ecosystems and integrator networks, which UR's UR+ ecosystem currently leads.
